skill.name: caveman-explore
skill.description: Read-only repository explorer. Use PROACTIVELY for cold-start exploration, broad cross-file localization, or when a direct search has failed and you need to find where something lives. Skip it when the issue already names the exact file or symbol, or a previous turn already returned usable file:line evidence. Returns only compact path:line citations; its reads and greps never enter the main conversation.
skill.summary: Locate relevant repository code quickly and return concise file and line citations.
skill.author: juliusbrussee

security_audit.summary: All four static findings are false positives in tests that validate the skill document. The skill is read-only, declares only Read, Glob, and Grep tools, and contains no semantic security concerns.

static_findings.snippet: assert.doesNotMatch(md, new RegExp("\\b" + marker + "\\b", "i"), `artifact must not contain ${marker
assert.match(md, /never edit|never.*solve|read-only/i, "must forbid editing and solving");

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 42 uses a JavaScript template literal only as an assertion message. It does not execute a shell command or invoke Ruby.
The import supports a test that reads the repository's local SKILL.md file. It provides no arbitrary path, write operation, or sensitive data access.
The synchronous read targets a fixed SKILL.md path derived from the test location. This is bounded test-fixture access with no user-controlled path or mutation.
Line 36 is a text assertion that requires the skill to forbid editing and solving. It performs no host discovery or system reconnaissance.

content.value_statement: Finding relevant code across an unfamiliar repository can consume time and context. This skill searches broadly and returns concise, verified file and line citations.
actual_capabilities: Searches repository paths, symbols, and text with read-only tools.
Runs complementary searches in parallel during initial exploration.
Reads promising files to verify relevant locations.
Returns compact file paths with verified line ranges.
Reports when no relevant locations are found.
limitations: Does not edit files or implement solutions.
Does not run shell commands, tests, or build tools.
Returns locations and relevance notes without detailed analysis.
Should not be used when exact files or symbols are already known.

use_cases.title: Orient in an unfamiliar codebase
use_cases.description: Locate entry points, related modules, and tests before planning a change.

use_cases.title: Trace a feature across files
use_cases.description: Find related definitions, handlers, configuration, and tests across repository boundaries.

use_cases.title: Gather evidence for delegated work
use_cases.description: Provide a solver with concise locations that reduce repeated repository searches.

prompt_templates.title: Find a named feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Find where [feature name] is implemented. Return only the most relevant file and line citations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner search for a known feature

prompt_templates.title: Locate implementation and tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Locate the implementation and tests for [symbol or behavior]. Include concise relevance notes with each citation.
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused exploration before a small change

prompt_templates.title: Map a cross-file workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Trace [workflow] from its entry point through major handlers and storage boundaries. Return verified citations in execution order.

prompt_templates.title: Compare competing hypotheses
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate whether [behavior] originates in [hypothesis A], [hypothesis B], or another location. Search broadly and cite only evidence that resolves the question.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced localization when direct searches failed

output_examples.input: Find where request routing selects a model.
output: src/router/pick.go:42-71 - route selection and model choice
src/router/pick_test.go:18-40 - table tests covering selection behavior

output_examples.input: Locate repository code for a feature that does not exist.

best_practices: Describe the behavior or symbol precisely enough to guide broad searches.
Use the returned citations as evidence before requesting implementation.
Delegate exploration early when the relevant repository area is unknown.
anti_patterns: Do not request file edits, commands, or complete solutions.
Do not use this skill when exact locations are already available.
Do not ask for speculative line ranges without repository evidence.

faq.question: Does this skill modify repository files?
faq.answer: No. It uses only Read, Glob, and Grep tools.

faq.question: Can it run tests or shell commands?
faq.answer: No. It cannot execute commands or test suites.

faq.question: What does the skill return?
faq.answer: It returns compact file and line citations with short relevance notes.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it for unfamiliar repositories, cross-file localization, or searches that did not find the relevant code.

faq.question: When should I skip it?
faq.answer: Skip it when the task already identifies the exact file, symbol, or usable citations.

faq.question: What happens when nothing relevant is found?
faq.answer: It reports that no relevant locations were found instead of guessing.
